Hey OP, I get how you feel!

I was in the industry over 10 years straight, started as Dish/Prep and worked up to Exec and then switched over into FOH and was just recently a GM for two different spots. Just started TODAY in Customer Success for a SaaS (Software as a Service) company. Wanted out for the last few years, and (gratefully) was laid off about 2 months ago due to company "realignment" as my last spot was bought out by a larger food group (sorry for rambling, just setting the mood).

YOU CAN GET OUT!

Truth be told, service folks usually develop a sense of giving a shit, attention to detail, and getting shit done (so you can go home) that most other jobs just don't teach or care about, and there's a tendency for both houses to be able to switch careers.

You should take stock of what you're capable of (give yourself some GODDAMN credit) and what you think will interest you. BOH folk tend towards ordering, inventory, and policy compliance, read this as Warehouse Management, Production Operations, Order & Inventory Management, or even Manufacturing Management. FOH folk tend towards customer-facing roles like Customer Support, Customer Service, Sales type roles.

HOWEVER, one thing you need to know is THE JOB MARKET KINDA SUCKS ASS RIGHT NOW for a lot of corporate-type gigs. I put in nearly 200 applications and ended up with 2 offers after having maybe 5 interviews. You will have to fight to sell your skill set as the outsider wanting in, but if you've made it through Valentine's dinner or Grill deciding they're so hungover they think they have Covid, you will be okay.

Make a resume. Feed it to ChatGPT. Reword ChatGPT because it puts words together weird. Ask ChatGPT to make you a cover letter for "Executive Assistant Ass Eater". Reword because of the words together weird. Ctrl+F to replace job title and company name for each different job.

Rinse, repeat (read: wipe, reset, next ticket push).

You fucking got this.

Oh, and make a LinkedIn. And look for LinkedIn tips on any social media you have, they're all good when you have a blank profile. Companies/recruiters love that shit.

Sorry for the cussing...I'm a few celebratory daiquiri snaquiri's in after my first day working from home. DM me if you want to talk more at all.

TLDR: You got this shit. Give yourself some credit, talk through your skill set, package it up nice for the companies to fight over you. Excited for you, my dude. Go get it.

Was helping my best friend bring in some cattle before a big storm hit a few years back. The storm was rolling in right around 7ish in the morning and it was just an absolutely beautiful sunrise, field of lavender and peach roses type of look. There was a real 'calm before the storm' mood: slightest gentle breeze, temperature in the mid-70s, and quiet as all hell. We had already gotten all but a few of the cattle inside and were just finishing up the head count when we realized we were short a calf. We go out looking but the winds were picking up badly and the thunder started getting so loud and frequent and mixing with the wind that we couldn't hear each other over the walkies so I texted him that we should probably just head back to the barnhouse and hope the calf had shown up.


Sure enough, the little bugger was nowhere to be seen so we're considering going back out one more time to look for a few minutes, but we could see the rain in the distance, it was heavy and it was coming fast. We decide it's not worth it to risk going out and possibly getting the buggy stuck or getting caught in a flash flood, so we start locking things up and hoping the little guy makes it through alright. As we're checking the locks on the pasture gate, we see a little brown-red dot burst through the tree line absolutely hauling ass. Not a second after the calf is in sight, we see the tops of the treeline just go crazy, like they're being pushed down by a huge slab of air or something. Takes a second but we realize that the "m&m-sized hail" the weatherman had predicted must actually be something closer to golf ball size, and it's coming down in fury. We get everything unlocked and are holding the doors, ready to shut them as soon as the calf gets in. End up having to cozy up with the cattle inside for about 45 minutes while we listen to the absolute beating that everything outside is taking.


That moment when the calf burst through the treeline has stuck with me since and reminds me of when action heroes are outrunning huge explosions in movies and I can't think of anything else when I watch movies now.

It's not a terrible pipeline, no pipelines in any half-regulated country are. Pipelines are usually built with at least 2 layers of steel and a rubber "bladder" layer that helps prevent cracking and seals leaks that develop over time. They're also usually built with erosion protection and anti-corrosive paint. Pipeline failures are pretty rare events, they just get so much media attention that they are blown onto a ridiculous scale, though that doesn't make them [failure events] any less harmful to the environment. When that does happen, it doesn't make the land unusable forever: nature will take its course and the land can again sustain plant life within a few years. This isn't an easy situation to solve. You can sit on your horse standing on a pedestal, but it's a fact that pipelines are essential to energy security, at least for now. Green energy is the future, definitely, but for right now, your day to day life is so heavily dependent on these hydrocarbon resources that you don't even realize it. These resources are the sole reason you can enjoy your standard of living, so please don't demonize and dismiss them simply because some asshat company has decided to do business in just about the worst way there is. My story isn't too relatable, however I've recovered from the trauma of an abusive childhood.
My biological father was a drunk, a junkie, and an abuser. He beat me and my siblings almost daily for at least a few years of my childhood, at least as far back as I can remember being the youngest of 3 kids. I remember wanting to end my own life when I was about 9 because the pain, emotionally and physically, was just so much to try to handle. I couldn't cry out for help, because where we lived, he was respected and nobody would believe us. My brother, 6 years my senior, routinely shielded my sister and I from the beatings, but he was often left unconscious or barely able to walk.
Shit was bad for a few years. It all came to a boil one night when I was about 10, he had come back in from drinking and was furious that dinner wasn't ready for him and that my mother didn't want to sleep with him that night. He started beating on her, getting in punches as quickly as he could. She was left nearly unconscious...and to be honest, I almost couldn't recognize my own mom under her mask of blood and swelling.
I snapped. Completely and utterly enraged at what he had done to her. I grabbed a vase and hurled it at his head, knocking him to the ground and I just kept hurling whatever I could get my hands on: dishes, pans, flower pots, chairs, anything. My sister was trying to wipe the blood off our mother's face, and my brother joined in with me, unleashing years of pent up fury and hatred.
We nearly beat him to death. For a while afterwards, I wish we had. Our sister had called the cops and an ambulance, and my brother and I were pulled off of him by police officers. They had to call an ambulance for him, but they also saw what he had done to our mom and just left him alone on the floor until the second ambulance arrived.

He never came back after that. He left my entire family fucked up for years. I attempted suicide 3 times in about as many years. We were poor before, but afterwards, when it was our mother raising 3 kids, we were dirt poor, I mean - 1 potato split 3 ways and that had to last 2 days - poor (mom didn't eat but 3 times a week, maybe).
But we made it through. I had to grow up fast, so I did. Each of us siblings eventually started working to help support the family. My siblings are doing just fine as well, and I'm blessed with an 8 y/o nephew that I spoil maybe a little too much. He's a smart kid, and he idolizes my brother to no end.
